fx._doc: Monkey Bananas runtime FX. Owner: Technical Artist. Consumer: Game Developer (texture-baker.ts createFxPlayer, or your own loader via resolveEmitter). Shape follows gamestudio particle-and-fx-authoring/references/fx-data-schema.md, with these project extensions: 'count' is the burst size passed to emitter.explode(count, x, y); 'bindings' map config fields (or 'count') to feel-tunable keys in src/core/tuning.ts, so tuning.ts stays the single source of truth and the numbers written here are fallbacks equal to today's tunables; 'spread' turns a bound scalar into a {min,max} of +/- that fraction; 'arc' builds the angle range (Phaser angles: 0 = right, 90 = down, 270 = straight up); 'tintChars' are PALETTE chars resolved at runtime (exact palette colours, no hex duplicated here); 'pixelSnap' is the render grid in logical px (= the particle's integer scale, README per-sprite snap rule); 'reducedMotion' may only disable an emitter or scale its count (countFactor = number or a tuning key). Every emitter: texture mb_atlas, blend NORMAL (no ADD: it would break the batch and push colours off-palette), constant integer scale (no scale-over-life: no fractional pixel art), no rotation (rotated pixel art crawls), fade by alpha only. Emitters live at (0,0) and burst at world coordinates. 'events' are cross-references only (fireFromFx false): the gameplay event wiring in motion/event-markers.md already fires the cue and the shake, so the FX player never double-fires them.

budget.targetDevice: min-spec mobile (2019 mid-range Android, Mali-G52 class), 60 fps
budget.gameplayMaxAliveTotal_note: Sum of maxAliveParticles over every gameplay emitter (tap 40 + critChips 32 + critSparks 16 + goldChips 16 + goldSparks 8 + confetti 36 + dust 12 = 160). evolvePoof is a flipbook (<= 24 sprites) and runs under the evolve input lock.
budget.drawCalls: 0 extra: every emitter uses mb_atlas + NORMAL blend + the default quad batch, so particles join the same batch as the sprites and text around them
budget.worstCaseSustained: 16 taps/s with Lucky Peel (10% crit) and a golden catch: about 17 tap chips + 7 crit chips + 3 crit sparks + 24 golden = 51 alive, 0.006 Mpx/frame
budget.odSevev_note: od-sevev adds ballotConfetti 24 (ceremony input lock, runs alone) + dustPuff 8 + inkSpecks 12 = 44 alive at most, inside the 160-sprite pool. The coin-burst (motion-spec coin-burst: a 16 fps spin per coin) is NOT a particle emitter, because the player gives each particle one static frame: it runs as the engine's pooled per-coin tween with its own cap of 36 alive (animator budget), 36 Sprite2D, one texture per spin frame (prop_coin0-3). Everything uses flat NORMAL-blend sprites; no ADD blend anywhere.

fx.trigger: Big Banana tap registered (pointer-down f0; keyboard: banana centre with the floater jitter). Not fired for dropped taps (> 16/s).
fx.vehicle_rationale: 3 tiny chips at up to 16 bursts/s: a pooled particle burst is the cheapest thing that reads; a flipbook would need 16 concurrent sprites.

costs.particlePx: 8x8 (2x2 particle_chip at x4 = the feel-spec 2x2 art-px footprint, on the art grid)

fx.trigger: crit tap (replaces tapChips for that pointer-down)
fx.vehicle_rationale: Same chip language as the tap, bigger and louder (x4 chips on the art grid, wider arc) plus a ring of sparkles so the crit reads in a 200 ms glance even with the floater on top.
A radial gold burst is the reward beat; particle_gold is hue-reserved for this FX only (style-guide). Light gravity so the gold hangs longer than tap chips (reward reads as special, not as debris).

fx.trigger: buy commit f0 (producer row, every hold-repeat tick) and upgrade commit f0
fx.anchor: the row icon centre in the shop
fx.vehicle_rationale: Small confetti pop that survives 10 buys/s hold-repeat without piling up (6 per buy, 36 alive cap). Colours are red, leaf-highlight and warm white only: yellow means bananas and blue is reserved for the intern (style-guide hue rules), so neither appears.

costs.particlePx: 8x8 (2x2 mask, one row or column lit, at x4)

fx.trigger: evolve-ceremony beat critters-poof: per visible critter, staggered start i x 180/max(N-1,1) ms (the developer schedules the stagger, one play() per critter)
fx.vehicle_rationale: The Animator specifies an exact 3-frame puff at 60 ms/frame; the silhouette is art-directed and frame-locked to the fanfare, so a flipbook is exact where particles would only approximate it. Cost: at most 24 pooled sprites for 180 ms, zero particles.

events.ref: evolveConfirm (fires once at t=0 for the whole ceremony)

fx.trigger: critter plop landing (buy flow, event-markers frame 7 / 120 ms after commit)
fx.anchor: critter feet (bottom-centre pivot of the new critter)
fx.vehicle_rationale: Two puffs, one each side, sliding out along the ground; separate left/right emitters guarantee the pair is symmetric (a single random-angle emitter can send both the same way).

fx.trigger: election ceremony IMPACT (rollEnd): crit.f5 sting, motion-spec.yaml election ceremony
fx.vehicle_rationale: 24 identical slips thrown once, under the ceremony input lock: one pooled burst is the cheapest thing that reads. Slips are pre-coloured white/paper sprites (fx_slip, fx_slip_tilt), so no tint and no off-palette colour. Flutter is approximated by two sprite orientations and low gravity; a true x-sine flutter needs a player feature (requested of the developer, optional).

events.ref: electionFanfare (the crash is inside the fanfare)

fx.trigger: the Magician lands from a zip (state-graph-magician land on_entry, returnZip/returnQuick → land)
fx.anchor: the Magician's feet (magicianFeet in sprites.json, world space)
fx.vehicle_rationale: Two puffs each side sliding out along the floor, like the fork's critterSpawnDust; separate emitters keep the pair symmetric.

fx.trigger: a rubber stamp lands (stamp_tool_down contact frame: paid / postponed / pardon / blackout stamps)
fx.anchor: the stamp's contact point (ui-kit stamp_tool_down pivot, world space)
fx.vehicle_rationale: A few ink specks sell the slam in 250 ms; 1x1 and 2x1 ink sprites keep the palette exact.
